title: Replication and Trust in Science
text:
Replication is one of the most important safeguards in scientific research. When a study's results can be reproduced by independent teams using the same methods, confidence in those findings grows considerably. In recent years, however, several high-profile fields have struggled to replicate a surprising number of landmark experiments. Critics argue that small sample sizes, selective reporting and pressure to publish novel results have distorted the evidence base.

In response, many journals now require researchers to pre-register their hypotheses and analysis plans before collecting data. This practice makes it harder to change the criteria for success after the results are known. Supporters maintain that it does not stifle creativity but rather separates exploratory findings from confirmatory ones. Nevertheless, scientists continue to debate whether such reforms will fully restore public trust.

questions.text: According to the passage, what can increase confidence in a study's findings?
options: Independent teams reproducing the results using the same methods
Publishing only novel results in major journals
Reporting only the results that support the hypothesis

questions.text: What do many journals now require researchers to do before collecting data?
options: Pre-register their hypotheses and analysis plans
Replicate landmark experiments with new funding

questions.text: What can be inferred about the purpose of pre-registration?
options: It aims to reduce the chance that criteria are changed to fit the results
It guarantees that every finding will be replicated
It is only used in medical research

questions.text: What does the final sentence of the passage imply about public trust in science?
options: Reforms may help, but their success is still uncertain
Public trust has already been fully restored
Public trust depends only on journal policies
Scientists have stopped debating how to reform research

vocabulary.definition: to reproduce a study or experiment so that its results can be checked
protective measures that prevent errors or misuse
done to discover new ideas rather than to test a fixed hypothesis
to record a study plan publicly before the data are collected

paragraph_translations: La replicación es una de las salvaguardas más importantes de la investigación científica. Cuando equipos independientes pueden reproducir los resultados de un estudio utilizando los mismos métodos, la confianza en esos hallazgos aumenta considerablemente. Sin embargo, en los últimos años, varios campos muy conocidos han tenido dificultades para replicar un número sorprendente de experimentos emblemáticos. Los críticos sostienen que los tamaños de muestra pequeños, la presentación selectiva de resultados y la presión por publicar resultados novedosos han distorsionado la base de evidencia.

En respuesta, muchas revistas exigen ahora que los investigadores preregistren sus hipótesis y planes de análisis antes de recopilar datos. Esta práctica dificulta cambiar los criterios de éxito una vez conocidos los resultados. Quienes la apoyan sostienen que no sofoca la creatividad, sino que separa los hallazgos exploratorios de los confirmatorios. No obstante, los científicos siguen debatiendo si estas reformas restaurarán por completo la confianza del público.
